questions.question: When you drink alcohol faster:

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Your body removes alcohol faster.
The effects of alcohol are less serious.
You are less likely to get pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink alcohol faster, more of it builds up in your body. It is never safe to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Protect only your eyes.
Work as well as a face shield.
Give the same protection as a windshield.
Protect your entire face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not the rest of your face. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if the clothing is very loose and flaps in the wind.
Yes, if you wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if you wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Good clothing can reduce injuries in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants made of sturdy material that cover your arms and legs. They should fit snug so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries are reduced by:

options.text: Wearing a helmet.
Wearing a leather jacket.
Using the rear brake only.
Wearing goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is the best protection against injury in a crash.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make things more dangerous because they may tailgate you at higher speeds.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, the rider should:

options.text: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles.
Go faster.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not warn the passenger about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. You should leave more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: When riding over a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat to:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle if needed.
Let your legs absorb the shock.
Help other drivers see you better.
Get a better view of the uneven surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your legs absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs absorb some of the impact. This keeps the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
Easier to see than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light before you slow down or stop helps other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket if the weather is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
Wear shorts in warm weather.
Not worry about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of sturdy material when riding, even in warm weather. A jacket helps protect you and prevents dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It helps you see better ahead.
It makes your view worse.
It makes it hard to see past the vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing to see better and to make yourself more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for ways to squeeze through the stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes too quickly from behind.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise
Fresh air

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your BAC (blood alcohol content). Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers can keep you awake, but they do not reduce your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Increase their speed.
Reduce their speed.
Make sudden moves.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on slippery surfaces. Sudden moves on slippery roads can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: Maintain enough space between you and other vehicles:

options.text: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
So you can tailgate.
To let traffic counters accurately count you.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space between you and the vehicle ahead lets you stop or swerve if it stops suddenly. This space also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is a good idea to drag your feet.
Your toes should point downward.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced. Do not drag your feet or point your toes downward, as this may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can use them quickly if needed.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Use only the front brake.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Travel on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves.
questions.explanation: Ride safely on slippery surfaces by using both brakes if needed, reducing speed, and avoiding sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges, as these have less traction.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?

options.text: Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest
On the left handle grip
On the right handle grip

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: If in a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if it is done before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones prohibit all passing. You cannot pass by riding off the main road either.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing later than usual.
Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Expect slower acceleration, slower turns, and longer stopping distances. Ride more slowly, start braking sooner, use more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for larger gaps before turning or merging.

questions.question: What should you check before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Tire wear and tread
How much padding your seat has
How shiny your paint is
The wind direction

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire wear and tread
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When choosing where to ride in your lane, you should think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you
How many cars are ahead of you
Which position will make your trip shorter
Which position lets you pass more vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. You also need enough space around you to react safely.

questions.question: How can your body get rid of alcohol?

options.text: Only time
Drinking coffee
Exercising
Taking a cold shower

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There is no way to speed this up.

questions.question: What can gloves do?

options.text: Make it hard to control your motorcycle and should not be worn
Help other drivers see you
Give you a better grip on the handlebars
Provide no protection

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars
questions.explanation: Gloves help you grip the handlebars better. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic
Dangerous for riders
Hard to understand
Safer than riding on open roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous for riders
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many vehicles meet there, creating risk of crashes between riders and other drivers.
